name: Blackwood
iocPatterns: DNS queries with fixed packet sizes toward microsoft.com
Use of .txt extension to mask DLL files (e.g., comx3.dll.txt)
Exploitation of unencrypted HTTP update channels for WPS Office, Tencent QQ, and Sogou Pinyin
Risky certificate/binary execution in paths like \Program Files\Common Files\microsoft shared\TextConv\
recommendedActions: Implement strict controls over software update environments, particularly those using unencrypted HTTP for Chinese-localized apps.
Monitor and alert on non-standard User-Agent strings (e.g., Windows 98) attempting to access large public web properties.
Audit the network's DNS traffic for an unusual volume of queries or fixed packet sizes towards known large service providers like Microsoft.
Enforce strict enforcement on your organization’s Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) and PowerShell settings to block unauthorized configuration changes.
Monitor system directories for files that use .txt extensions but contain executables or are called by shell-bound processes.
Implement EDR rules to flag and intercept the execution of any DLL beyond established whitelist boundaries in System32 folders.
Perform periodic audits on local security products (e.g., 360 Safeguard) to verify that they have not been manipulated or altered for allowlisting.
Block outgoing traffic to known C&C proxy markers including specific high-numbered UDP ports like 4499 and 8000.
campaignsText: Blackwood's activity indicates a long-term, persistent threat profile characterized by stable infrastructure and well-tested malware lineages (Project Wood/DCM). The group exhibits organized operational tempo with consistent reuse of infrastructure obfuscation methods—specifically leveraging high-traffic platforms to mask C2. Their strategy targets specific regional software (WPS Office) used extensively in manufacturing systems, showing a focused approach rather than broad, undiscriminating spam.
description: Blackwood is a Chinese-aligned APT group that employs highly sophisticated, modular espionage tools and infrastructure obfuscation techniques. The group targets industrial and financial sectors in China, Japan, and the United Kingdom by leveraging supply chain compromises and adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) attacks to deliver the NSPX30 implant.
goals: The strategic objectives of Blackwood center on high-value economic espionage and intelligence gathering from industrial, commercial, and financial entities. The group focuses on infrastructure that facilitates international trade or manufacturing, specifically targeting organizations in China, Japan, and the United Kingdom. Their use of Chinese-specific application updates as a primary infection vector suggests a deliberate focus on targets with cross-border operations involving popular regional software.
